newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt issues sell, some stability seen.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt issues sell, some stability seen.

text.p: Issuance of $1.6 billion high-grade corporate debt found good demand at attractive levels on Thursday, while buyers reemerged in the secondary to provide some sense of stability, dealers said.
The host of high-yield issues priced on Wednesday and Thursday were mixed in secondary markets, meanwhile, reflecting a reserved buy-side, traders there said.

High-yield wireless cables were called steady after gaining on Wednesday, but traders said they expected losses for Heartland Wireless debt after the company late Thursday reported a fourth quarter EBITDA loss of $9.6 million.
Elsewhere, CAI Wireless Systems Inc debt was unchanged at 49-1/2 and bonds of People's Choice TV Corp were up 1/2 point to 41-1/2 to 42.
Paging Network Inc's 10 percent debt traded lower on Thursday before trimming losses, one trader said. The notes were quoted down 1/2 at 95-1/2, 96 at the close.

In new junk issues, Central Tractor Farm & Country Inc's $105 million 1-5/8 percent 10-year debt were quoted off on the bid near the close at 99-1/2. The notes priced at par to yield 389 basis points over the Treasury curve via NationsBanc Capital Markets Inc.

Bonds from recent issues were mixed. Borg-Warner Security Corp's 9-5/8 percent notes traded in a 99 to 99-1/4 market on Thursday compared with Wednesday's issue price of 99.334. Key Plastics Inc's 10-1/4 percent debt held gains achieved when freed to trade and closed at 100-1/2 to 100-3/4.

In the high-grade market, issuers were able to raise the size of some debt offerings in response to growing investor demand with long Treasury yields near seven percent, dealers said. Further, issues were priced at spreads five to 10 basis points wider than seen two weeks ago and were therefore called "priced to sell."

New issues included $750 million of debt in four tranches from Banc One Corp via Goldman, Sachs & Co, $200 million 30-year debt from Cooper Tire & Rubber via Merrill Lynch & Co, and $650 million 10put5 debt from Export-Import Bank of Korea via Lehman Brothers.
Buying in secondary paper improved on Thursday following what one trader referred to as "abysmal" demand this week.

"Today we're starting to see some bottom-fishers and we actually sold some paper today," the trader said. "In the quality industrials there's definitely some buyers. There's no real tightening but stability is what we wanted to see."
Tobacco debt was most active on Thursday in anticipation of an anti-smoking settlement that may reveal potentially damaging documents against the tobacco industry, traders said.
Tobacco spreads had already widened by five basis points on the week in a reversal of significant spread compression seen over the past few months, analysts said.
RJR Nabisco's 8-3/4s of 2007 were wider by 10 basis points on Thursday to 200 basis points over Treasuries.

In the Treasury market, prices ended mixed after a session of curve-flattening trades in reponse to what most players now believe will be a tightening of monetary policy. The moves came as Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan repeated the need to be preemptive in the fight against inflation.
The Federal Open Market Committee meets on March 25.
The 30-year bond closed up 12/32 to yield 6.96 percent.
